name: switch
purpose: Control-only pill toggle `Switch` (36×20 px). Two visual types: `default` (plain handle) and `privacy` (handle carries a `az-lock` / `az-lock-open` icon mirroring the toggled state; both glyphs render and `group-data-[checked]:` shows the right one, so no class is chosen in script). No label or description — wrap it in a horizontal `Field` or a `Field.Label` choice card for labeled layouts, or place it bare where the label already exists outside the control (an ItemGroup row names the field with `Item.Title`). Because the bare form has no wrapper to defer to, the control owns its own `disabled` state.
useWhen: Use Switch for any on/off setting that applies at once — the answer for 'toggle'. For an on/off choice submitted with a form use Checkbox; to switch a view or mode in place use ToggleGroup.
An on/off setting that takes effect as soon as it flips (enable a feature, turn a rule on).
A row that already names the setting outside the control, such as an `item` row whose title is the label.
A visibility or access toggle: `variant="privacy"` shows a closed lock when off and an open lock when on.
avoidWhen: The toggle needs its own label, description, or helper text in a form → wrap it in a horizontal `field` (`Field orientation="horizontal"` + `Field.Content`).
The toggle should sit in a bordered card with a description → use a `field` choice card (`Field.Label` wrapping a horizontal `Field`).
A text value that only applies while a feature is on → compose a `Field` with an `InputGroup` (`InputGroup.Input` + an `InputGroup.Addon` holding the switch).
The choice is submitted with a form instead of applied immediately → use `checkbox`.
related: `field` — a horizontal `Field` gives the switch its label and description; a `Field.Label` wrapping it is a card-style option.
`input-group` — a text input with a trailing switch addon that enables it, inside a `Field`.
`checkbox` — boolean selection submitted with a form.
`item` — list row whose title names a bare switch.
bestPractices: The switch renders no text: give it an accessible name with `aria-label`, or `aria-labelledby` pointing at the visible label.
Set `disabled` on the switch itself; it renders a native disabled button, so it leaves the tab order and ignores clicks and keys.
Use `autofocus` to focus the switch when it mounts (a dialog whose first control it is).
Keep `variant="default"` unless the setting is about visibility or access.

props.name: variant
props.doc: Visual variant (`SwitchVariant`). `privacy` renders a lock icon inside the handle (closed when off, open when on).

props.name: autofocus
props.doc: Moves focus to the switch once, when it mounts.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Disables interaction and applies the disabled tokens.

props.name: invalid
props.doc: Marks the control invalid: sets `aria-invalid` and the danger border (unchecked). An enclosing `Field`'s `invalid` sets it too.

props.name: name
props.doc: Form field name. Set, a hidden input inside the button submits `on` under this name while the switch is on and nothing while it is off, as a native checkbox does; `disabled` leaves it out.
